thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: SEV2 - prefill GPU OOMs detected in prod-west (rwd-infer-gpu-v4). Multiple containers restarting. Top stack: CudaOutOfMemory in prefill path. Auto-attach: logs and node metrics.

maya: oncall here, acked. jumping in. tagging @sahil and @tess for runtime + infra.

sahil: seeing repeated OOMs from prefill for requests with very large context windows (~60k tokens) and high prefetch counts. Containers go from running -> oom_kill -> restart in ~30s. grabbing crash dumps now.

tess: confirming node flaps on two nodes (gpu-nodex-07, gpu-nodex-09) around 03:42 UTC. kube events show containerd reporting OOM then kubelet restart.

kevin: FYI CS already flagged 2 paying customers seeing 5xx for generation endpoints. they want ETA.

sahil: quick hypothesis: prefill path is allocating full KV and prefetch buffers for long-context requests and batch merging pushes memory over threshold. Also a recent driver bump to CUDA 535.104 might make headroom tighter.

maya: immediate mitigation options? list quick wins.

ops: recommend throttling long-context requests at the proxy first. can we set a temporary max_context_tokens and disable prefetching?

sahil: yes. recommended rollout (immediate):
- set max_context_tokens=16000 for pool rwd-infer-gpu-v4
- disable prefetch/prefill for requests with header X-Disable-Prefetch!=true
- lower max_batch_tokens to 4096 for on-GPU pools
- enable fallback route to cpu-fallback-pool for overflow

maya: do it. tess, can infra apply proxy throttles and fallback routing?

tess: on it. applying rule now.

ops: running control-plane call to set overrides (example):
```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/pools/rwd-infer-gpu-v4/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prefetch_enabled":false,"max_context_tokens":16000,"max_batch_tokens":4096,"fallback_pool":"cpu-fallback-pool"}'
```

ops: rule posted, control-plane acknowledged, rolling to edge proxies.

tess: also pushed an envoy rate-limit config to limit requests with query param long_context=true to 10 r/s per tenant.

sahil: patching runtime to trim prefill buffers on allocate and early-evict KV if free_mem < 10%. quick patch landed to canary on one node with env PREFETCH_WORKER=0. Restarting canary container.

maya: customer comms? kevin?

kevin: sent short notice to affected customers: "We're investigating increased 5xx; temporary mitigations applied that may affect very large-context requests. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA." offering credit if impacted.

ops: monitoring: container restart rate down ~70% over last 3m. OOM traces no longer seen on canary.

sahil: logs from canary show prefill path now bailing with 503 and explicit "prefill disabled for >16000 tokens" instead of OOM. pushing same runtime flag to remaining nodes in 2m.

tess: rolling restarts scheduled carefully: drain node -> restart -> validate KV/prefetch metrics -> bring back. doing sequential to avoid capacity hole.

maya: great. setting postmortem owner: @sahil for root cause + runtime fix, @tess for infra remediation, @ops for runbook updates, @kevin for CS follow-ups.

incident-bot: ACTIONS: oncall handoff set to maya until 07:00 UTC. Runbook reference: https://wiki.internal/incidents/prefill-gpu-oom

kevin: customers acknowledged, one asked for more detail; will escalate if they want deeper technical writeup.

sahil: initial root cause assumption: prefetching + large-context batching + marginal driver memory regression. next steps: reproduce in staging with same driver and long-context workload, add safe-guards in runtime to pre-empt heavy prefill for single requests.

maya: closing on live incident thread for now, keep monitoring for 30m and post updates here. thanks team :thumbsup:

ops: monitoring note: set alert threshold to 5 restarts/min per pool to avoid noise.

last: canary metrics look stable. will open postmortem ticket with timeline and mitigations.
